title: Utility Order for Southwestern Electric Power Company, ex parte. — Order No. U-37463 accepts the Uncontested Stipulated Settlement which certified the Hallsville CT project and the Welsh Plant conversion subject to the conditions within. This matter was considered at the September 16, 2026 Business and Executive Session.

documents.text:
LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                  ORDER NUMBER U-37463

             SOUTHWESTERN ELECTRIC POWER COMPANY, EX PARTE.

Docket No. U-37463, In re: Application for approval to construct the Hallsville natural gas plant
and to convert the Welsh Units 1 and 3 to natural gas.

             (Decided at the September 16, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)


                                            ORDER

 I.     BACKGROUND

        On December 18, 2024, Southwestern Electric Power Company, (“SWEPCO” or

 “Company”) filed its Application with the Louisiana Public Service Commission (“LPSC” or

 “Commission”) for approval to construct the Hallsville natural gas plant and to convert the

 Welsh Units 1 and 3 to natural gas. (“Application”). The Application was supported by written

 testimony with exhibits on behalf of the Company consisting of the sworn testimony of Melissa

 Gage, James F. Martin, Jay Godfrey, Michael Dilley, Jacob Miller, Noah Hollis, Hassan Hayat,

 Matthew DeCoursey, and Gary Spitznogle.

        Notice of the Company’s Application was published in the Commission’s Official

 Bulletin No. 1339 on December 20, 2024 with a 25-day intervention period. No interventions

 were received.

        On January 15, 2025, the docket was assigned to Administrative Law Judge (“ALJ”)

 Joy Guillot. A status conference was held on February 18, 2025. The parties thereafter agreed

 to a procedural schedule and an order was issued on February 25, 2025 setting a procedural

 schedule.

        Several sets of data requests were submitted by Staff to the Company and the Company

 responded timely. Staff filed the Direct Testimony of Jonathan R. Bourg on June 17, 2025. In

 summary, Staff recognized that, assuming SWEPCO discontinues operation of Welsh as a

 coal-fired generating facility, SWEPCO would face a significant capacity shortfall beginning in

 2028. Staff concluded that the Hallsville natural gas facility and the proposed Welsh conversion

 to natural gas would fill this need by providing critically needed firm capacity. Staff concluded

 that SWEPCO had sufficiently and materially followed the Commission’s Market Based

 Mechanism Order (“MBM Order”) in procuring the resources to the satisfaction of Staff and

 the Independent Monitor (“IM”) and that the construction of the 450 MW Hallsville CT project


                                                                              Order No. U-37463
                                                                                         Page 1
 and gas conversion of Welsh Units 1 and 3 were reasonable and prudent and served the

publicconvenience and necessity, and represented the lowest reasonable cost to ratepayers from

the bids received. Staff recommended that a Commission approval be subject to the following

three conditions: (1) that the Commission require SWEPCO to initiate a prudence proceeding

within 180 days of Commercial Operation Date (“COD”) for each project so that the

Commission can review actual cost and initial operating performance of the facilities; (2) that

that SWEPCO be required to identify in Energy Cost Recovery (“ECR”) Rider filings for the

first five operating years the gas commodity and transportation costs associated with the

Hallsville CTs and the Welsh gas units; (3) that the Commission require SWEPCO to provide

quarterly updates to the Commission regarding the construction activities for each facility.

       On August 18, 2025, SWEPCO filed the Rebuttal Testimony of Melissa Gage. In

summary, the Rebuttal Testimony agreed with Staff’s recommended conditions, except that

SWEPCO be required to identify in FAC filings rather than in rider filings for the first five

operating years the gas commodity and transportation costs associated with the Hallsville CTs

and the Welsh gas units, and cost recovery for the projects would be through SWEPCO’s

Generation Recovery Rider (“GRR”).           After extensive negotiations, Staff agreed with

SWEPCO’s proposed change to the conditions.

       On July 17, 2026, SWEPCO and Staff entered into an Uncontested Stipulated

Settlement. This executed Settlement was filed into the record, as part of the Joint Motion to Set

an Uncontested Stipulated Settlement Hearing on July 27, 2026, with written settlement

testimony of Lynn Ferry-Nelson on behalf of SWEPCO and the settlement testimony of

Jonathan R. Bourg on behalf of Staff. A hearing on the Settlement was held on August 24, 2026

before Administrative Law Judge Joy Guillot.


II.    COMMISSION AUTHORITY

       The Commission exercises jurisdiction in this proceeding pursuant to Article IV, Sec.
21 of the Louisiana Constitution.
       La. Const. Art. IV. Sec. 21 provides in pertinent part:

              The Commission shall regulate all common carriers and
              public utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided
              by law. It shall adopt and enforce reasonable rules, regulations
              and procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties, and shall
              have other powers and perform other duties as provided by law.

III.   STIPULATED SETTLEMENT

                                                                                Order No. U-37463
                                                                                           Page 2
      The Settlement resolves all issues in this proceeding. Terms of the Settlement are:




Approval of the Application
(a) Approval of the Hallsville Natural Gas Plant. The Settling Parties request that the
   Commission approve the relief requested by SWEPCO in its Application. In furtherance
   of this request, the parties agree that the 450 MW nameplate Hallsville CT Project is in the
   public interest and adheres to the applicable regulations and law.


(b) Approval of the Welsh Plant Conversion. The Settling Parties request that the Commission
   approve the relief requested by SWEPCO in its Application. In furtherance of this request,
   the parties agree that the conversion of the Welsh Plant from coal to natural gas is in the
   public interest and adheres to the applicable regulations and law.


(c) Need for the Plants. The Settling Parties agree that the Plants are needed to serve the public
   interest as SWEPCO is projected to experience a significant winter capacity deficit by
   Planning Year 2028/2029. The Hallsville Natural Gas Plant and Welsh Plant Conversion
   will account for approximately 1300 MW of accredited winter capacity to address
   SWEPCO’s load requirements.


(d) Cost Recovery. The Settling Parties agree that initial recovery of the costs associated with
   the Hallsville Project and the Welsh conversion is allowed through its Generation Recovery
   (GRR) Rider previously approved by the Commission in Order U-36385-A. SWEPCO
   will be allowed to include the estimated first-year revenue requirement of the Hallsville
   CT Project and Welsh Plant Conversion in its GRR Rider effective on the date of the first
   billing cycle after each of the power generation facilities begins providing service to
   customers, subject to Commission review and reconciliation in the utility’s next rate
   proceeding and in the prudence proceeding required to be initiated by this Stipulation, as
   prescribed by the settlement agreement and order approving the agreement in Docket No.
   U-37502. SWEPCO will file with the Commission updated factors for its GRR prior to
   each of the generation facilities providing service to customers.


   In the first SWEPCO FRP proceeding covering the first full test year period that the GRR
   Rider reflected the revenue requirement of the generating assets, SWEPCO shall adjust its
   FRP so that recovery of the Hallsville CT Project and Welsh Plant Conversion is reflected
   within the Company’s FRP mechanism. The Hallsville CT Project and Welsh Plant
   Conversion revenue requirements will then be removed from the GRR Rider rates
   contemporaneous with implementation of these new FRP rates as prescribed in LPSC
   Docket No. U-37502-A, Order dated April 7, 2026. For example, if one of the plants comes
   online in December of 2027, the first full test year the plant would be in service would be



                                                                             Order No. U-37463
                                                                                        Page 3
    2028, and it would then be moved to the Formula Rate Plan with the 2029 filing or would
   remain in the GRR Rider if the Formula Rate Plan is not in effect.


   The Company will be required to true-up any differences between the estimated first year
   revenue requirement included in the GRR Rider and the actual revenue requirement during
   that period (including actual expenses reflected in that revenue requirement). Such true-
   up shall account for the period of over-collection or under-collection based on the
   difference in projected revenue requirement and actual requirement with a one-time credit
   or charge reflected in the GRR Rider.


   Fuel expense will flow through the Company’s Fuel Adjustment Clause (FAC), subject to
   Commission Review. SWEPCO’s proposed depreciable life of 30 years for the Hallsville
   Natural Gas Plant is reasonable. The Settling Parties also agree that each of the Welsh Units
   will have a depreciable life of 15 years after the units are converted and placed in-service.


(e) MBM Order Compliance. The Settling Parties agree that SWEPCO conducted its Request
   for Proposals (RFP) for the Plants in compliance with the Commission’s MBM Order.


(f) 1983 Order Compliance. The Settling Parties agree that SWEPCO’s Application for
   Certification of the Plants meets the requirements of the Commission’s 1983 Order, by
   demonstrating that the Hallsville Natural Gas Plant and Welsh Plant Conversion will serve
   the public need and necessity.


(g) Compliance with Order U-36385-A. The Settling Parties agree that SWEPCO’s issuance
   of Requests for Proposals (RFP) in this proceeding meets the requirements of Order No.
   U-36385-A, as SWEPCO included a PPA RFP.


Commitments
(a) Prudence Review. The Settling Parties agree that, in accordance with Staff’s
   recommendation, SWEPCO will initiate a single prudence proceeding including both the
   Hallsville and Welsh facilities within 180 days of all facilities reaching commercial
   operation to allow for Commission review. The prudence filing shall be supported by
   sworn testimony from the company detailing, at a minimum, the expected construction cost
   of the facility (and the components thereof) compared to the actual construction costs of
   the facilities, any changes to the O&M expenses estimated at the time of filing, deviations
   from the schedule as originally contemplated, any changes to the design of the plant during
   construction that may modify performance or reliability, and any other changes in
   circumstances from the assumptions and expectations included in the Company’s filing.


(b) Fuel Adjustment Clause (FAC). The Settling Parties agree that, for the first five operating
   years, SWEPCO shall specifically identify the gas commodity and transportation costs
   associated with the Plants in its FAC Rider filings.

                                                                           Order No. U-37463
                                                                                      Page 4
    (c) Informational Updates
          a. Continuing Updates of Significant Events. The Company will keep the
               Commission updated on significant events related to the approval proceedings in
               other jurisdictions by filing updates in this Docket as needed.


          b. Quarterly Reports. Beginning on September 1, 2026, and quarterly thereafter, until
               the Plants are fully operational, the Company will provide Quarterly Informational
               Updates to the Commission regarding construction and conversion activities for
               the Plants. This reporting will contain the information reflected in Exhibit JRB-10.


   Discovery and Motions
       The Settling Parties acknowledge that there are no pending requests for discovery or
motions pending before either the Commission or the Administrative Law Judge.


   General Reservations


       The Settling Parties represent and agree that, except as specifically otherwise provided
       here:


       (a) This Joint Stipulation and Term Sheet represents a negotiated settlement for the
          purposes of settling all issues which were raised relating to this proceeding.


       (b) Each of the undersigned counsel of record affirmatively represents that he or she has
          full authority to execute this Joint Stipulation and Term Sheet on behalf of their
          client(s).


       (c) None of the signatories hereto shall be prejudiced or bound by the terms of the Joint
          Stipulation and Term Sheet in the event the Commission does not approve this Joint
          Stipulation and Term Sheet nor shall any of the Settling Parties be prejudiced or bound
          by the terms of this Joint Stipulation and Term Sheet should any appeal of a
          Commission order adopting this Joint Stipulation and Term Sheet be filed with the
          courts.


       (d) Nothing contained herein shall constitute an admission by any Settling Party that any
          allegation or contention in these proceedings as to any of the foregoing matters is true
          or valid and shall not in any respect constitute a determination by the Commission as
          to the merits of any allegations or contentions made in this proceeding.


       (e) The Settling Parties agree that the provisions of this Joint Stipulation and Term Sheet
          are the result of extensive negotiations, and the terms and conditions of this Joint
          Stipulation and Term Sheet are interdependent. The Settling Parties agree that settling
                                                                                 Order No. U-37463
                                                                                            Page 5
            the issues in this Joint Stipulation and Term Sheet is in the public interest and, for that
           reason, they have entered into this Joint Stipulation and Term Sheet to settle among
           themselves the issues in this Joint Stipulation and Term Sheet. This Joint Stipulation
           and Term Sheet shall not constitute nor be cited as a precedent nor deemed an
           admission by any Settling Party in any other proceeding except as necessary to enforce
           its terms before the Commission or any state court of competent jurisdiction. The
           Commission’s decision, if it enters an order consistent with this Joint Stipulation and
           Term Sheet, will be binding as to the matters decided regarding the issues described in
           this Joint Stipulation and Term Sheet, but the decision will not be binding with respect
           to similar issues that might arise in other proceedings. A Settling Party’s support of
           this Joint Stipulation and Term Sheet may differ from its position or testimony in other
           dockets. To the extent there is a difference, the Settling Parties are under no obligation
           to take the same position as set out in this Joint Stipulation and Term Sheet in other
           dockets.


   Non-Severability
       The Settling Parties agree that the agreements contained in this Joint Stipulation and Term
Sheet have resulted from negotiations among the Settling Parties and are interrelated and
interdependent. The Settling Parties hereto specifically state and recognize that this Joint
Stipulation and Term Sheet represents a balancing of positions of each of the Settling Parties in
consideration for the agreements and commitments made by the other Settling Parties in
connection therewith. Therefore, in the event that the Commission does not approve and adopt the
terms of this Joint Stipulation and Term Sheet in total and without modification or condition
(provided, however, that the affected party or parties may consent to such modification or
condition), this Joint Stipulation and Term Sheet shall be void and of no force and effect, and no
Settling Party shall be bound by the agreements or provisions contained herein. The Settling Parties
agree that neither this Joint Stipulation and Term Sheet nor any of the provisions hereof shall
become effective unless and until the Commission shall have entered an Order approving the terms
and provisions as agreed by the parties to this Joint Stipulation and Term Sheet and such Order
becomes final and non-appealable.

 IV.    COMMISSION CONSIDERATION

        This matter was considered at the Commission’s September 16, 2026 Business and

 Executive Session. After discussion, on motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by

 Commissioner Francis, and unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to accept the

 Uncontested Stipulated Settlement filed into the record on July 27, 2026.

 IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED THAT:
   1) The Uncontested Stipulated Settlement filed into the record on July 27, 2026 is
      accepted; and
   2) This order is effective immediately.


BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
